## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials in this search yet. In generation 0, 84 trials in 7 worlds all scored exactly 0, on dev and in training, and no recipe or network family made a difference. So the agent is failing to learn at all, not failing to generalise. Seed noise cannot be measured yet. The settings never tried are n_envs above 256, lr above 2e-3, gae_lambda below 0.9 and networks smaller than the starting one. This world may also differ from its description in some hidden way, for example in how action indices map to grid cells. This round therefore runs three different probes rather than small refinements: (1) the starting network with a recipe at the untried extremes; (2) a small network with exact footprint convolutions and a DONE head that sees the whole board directly; (3) the starting network plus a layout-free dense placement path, so the agent can fix any index-to-cell mismatch.

### Round 2
Including generation 0, 87 trials have all scored 0 on both training and dev success, and they span very different architectures and recipes. When everything scores 0, seed noise cannot be measured and no idea can be ranked against another. Because the results do not depend on the network, the cause is probably shared by all runs. Three causes have not been tested yet. (1) The reward may be sparse or delayed, which would need almost Monte Carlo credit assignment (gamma 0.995, lambda 0.99, full-episode rollouts). (2) DONE or the actions may sit at indices the conv head misses. A linear path from the observations to every action, DONE included, plus a learned bias per action, could adapt to this. (3) The reward scale may be large, so value gradients dominate the global gradient-norm clip and starve the policy. A separate critic still shares the clip, so this was never really tested. Shrinking the critic's gradient tests it directly.

### Round 3
Every trial so far has scored 0 for training and dev success, across about 90 trials in two generations. That includes the extreme recipes (n_envs 1024, lr 3e-3, lambda 0.8, near Monte Carlo returns), dense paths that can learn any action layout, a DONE path read from the board, and a critic whose gradient was scaled down. A conv policy with dense shaping should learn something, so the world probably differs in reward scale, input scale or optimiser balance rather than in network capacity or action layout. Two robustness fixes have never been tried. (1) A zero critic: normalised advantages make the policy gradient independent of reward scale, and no value loss can use up the shared gradient-norm clip. (2) Normalisation layers after the first learned layer, plus orthogonal initialisation with a near-uniform starting policy, which guard against odd input scales. These three candidates form a 2x2 test of the two fixes. All three use the same recipe.

### Round 4
All 9 trials in this search scored 0 on both seeds, with 0 training success. That includes extreme recipes, layout-free paths, a separate or zero critic, and normalisation. Generation 0 also scored 0 in every world. With everything at zero, no idea can be ranked against another. One explanation fits every failure regardless of network or recipe: the agent may learn to press DONE immediately. Random placements put most cells outside the target, so early returns are negative, while DONE returns 0. DONE is a single action whose logit is easy to raise, so it could take over before placement skills form. The episode then ends at once and exploration stops. A -2 DONE bias at the start (tried in generation 0) would only delay this, not prevent it. This round tests that idea in three ways: a strong fixed penalty on the DONE logit, a slowed-down DONE logit, and a DONE logit that depends on how much of the target looks unfinished.
